1.explanation: All of these files define and configure the Pagination component that is used in the DataTable example. The vanilla JS files (packages/components/src/components/pagination/*.js) contain the core logic and markup for rendering the select dropdown of pages. The React wrapper (packages/react/src/components/Pagination/Pagination.js and its index.js) exposes that pagination API to Carbon-React users. Because the unwanted Select list behavior originates in these files, they must be updated (for example, adding a NumberInput alternative or making the dropdown virtualized) to fix the issue across all usages.
1.bug_scenario: On DataTablePagination the built-in Pagination component renders its “go to page” as a Select with one entry per page. With 69+ pages the Select grows well beyond the viewport and the list of page numbers overflows the browser, forcing the user to scroll up and down inside the dropdown just to find a page. The user cannot quickly type in a page number, making it unsuitable for tables with many pages.

2.explanation: These files collectively generate and render the page‐selector dropdown in the Pagination component. In the React package (packages/react/src/components/Pagination), Pagination.js (and its index.js export) builds the <Select> element and the list of page options. In the core components library (packages/components/src/components/pagination), pagination.config.js defines default settings (like CSS class names and default props) and pagination.js calculates total pages and constructs the array of page options. To switch from a long dropdown to a number input, or to constrain the height of the dropdown, you must modify these files where the page-options array is generated and where the <Select> is rendered.
2.bug_scenario: The Pagination component’s page selector uses a dropdown <Select>. When you have many pages (for example, 650 rows at 10 per page → 69 pages), clicking the selector opens a very tall list of page numbers that extends beyond the browser viewport, forcing the user to scroll within the dropdown to find a page like 60. This is poor UX and not acceptable.
